clue.text: He has combined forces to free legionaries' Sergeant- Major

indicators.note: freeing the letters lets them break formation and line up again in a new order

parts.note: SM is the standard abbreviation for Sergeant Major

explanation.surface: A commander liberates the legionaries' senior NCO.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to free' signals the anagram of LEGIONARIES plus SM. The definition is cryptic: a supreme commander heads combined (allied) forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme commander, especially one leading several armies at once, is the person in charge of combined forces.

clue.text: Sociability shown by Robin at sea

parts.note: Robin Goodfellow is the mischievous sprite Puck of English folklore
a ship is what is found at sea

explanation.surface: A sailor named Robin is good company aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Goodfellow is another name for Puck, the sprite of English folklore and A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly companionship is the warmth of being good company.

clue.text: Vienna evidently infiltrated by moles

indicators.note: the answer sits concealed inside the words, as spies infiltrate

explanation.walkthrough: 'moles' suggests spies, matching 'infiltrated'; here they are skin blemishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi are birthmarks, such as skin blemishes of the raised dark kind.

clue.text: Museum sets poser to one party member

indicators.note: sets as in sets out or arranges, so these letters are placed in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A museum gives a puzzle to a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets' rearranges POSER into REPOS.
explanation.definitionFit: A place where objects are stored and displayed is a storehouse or museum.

clue.text: Information base

explanation.definitionFit: The inside story is the facts, and a mean trick is despicable or dishonourable.

clue.text: Oarsmen on course — the fewer the better

definitions.meaning: the rowers who set the pace in a boat

definitions.text: on course — the fewer the better
definitions.meaning: shots counted on a golf course, where a low score wins

explanation.definitionFit: The rower nearest the stern sets the rhythm, and golfers count every shot, wanting as few as possible.

clue.text: This kind of wheel doesn't work

definitions.meaning: a gear wheel that only transmits motion between two others

explanation.definitionFit: An intermediate gear is named for doing no work itself, and a jobless person is inactive.

clue.text: Something indispensable to the composer

parts.note: a musical part the composer marks as essential, not to be left out

explanation.walkthrough: The Italian term means obligatory, the opposite of ad libitum.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrumental part a composer requires to be played is marked with an Italian word for obligatory.

clue.text: Machinery for testing those in retirement needing a rise

definitions.text: Machinery for testing those in retirement needing a rise

parts.words: Machinery for testing those in retirement needing a rise
parts.note: those who retire go to bed, so a bed frame that rises: the test rig for vertical take-off jets

explanation.walkthrough: 'retirement' suggests old age; it means going to bed. The 1950s Rolls-Royce vertical take-off test rig had this nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s Rolls-Royce test rig for vertical take-off was nicknamed for its resemblance to a bed frame that rises.

clue.text: Beat — six delivered with energy

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls delivered by one bowler
power is energy, force

explanation.surface: A batsman hits a six off a fierce delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: An OVER is the set of six balls a cricket bowler delivers in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat an opponent is to defeat or subdue them.

clue.text: Lincoln's Inn we hear, two pounds a ticket

indicators.note: the word 'Inn' when spoken sounds like 'in', telling us one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra), so two of them give LL
Abe is the first name of Abraham Lincoln, US president

explanation.surface: Lincoln's Inn, one of London's legal societies, charging two pounds for a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln's Inn is one of London's four Inns of Court for barristers; 'Inn we hear' sounds like 'in', putting ABE inside the two Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a tag or tab attached to goods, much like a small tag or docket.

clue.text: They are buttoned up for a fight

definitions.text: They are buttoned up for a fight

parts.words: They are buttoned up for a fight
parts.note: not combatants wearing tight jackets, but fencing swords tipped with protective buttons for a bout

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttoned up' suggests people in fastened coats; fencing swords carry a button on the tip for safety.
explanation.definitionFit: Light fencing swords carry a blunt button on the point so bouts are safe.

clue.text: Race of giants

definitions.meaning: a classic flat horse race run at Epsom for fillies
huge, long-lived trees of the forest

explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is an English classic horse race for fillies at Epsom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Epsom classic for fillies takes its name from an estate, and great forest trees can be called giants.

clue.text: Not an airborne soldier from overseas

definitions.text: Not an airborne soldier from overseas

parts.words: Not an airborne soldier from overseas
parts.note: the flightless national bird of New Zealand is also the nickname of a New Zealander, including a soldier

explanation.walkthrough: 'Airborne soldier' suggests a paratrooper; the clue means a flightless bird and a New Zealand serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: New Zealanders, soldiers included, are nicknamed after their flightless national bird.

clue.text: Salt water for a Piscean as arranged

indicators.note: the letters are arranged afresh, put into a new order

explanation.surface: Sea water suits someone born under the fish sign, as you'd expect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' signals the anagram of A PISCEAN plus AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest inland body of water, between Europe and Asia, is a saline lake.

clue.text: Answer to space in Fleet Street — reduce weight

definitions.text: Answer to space in Fleet Street
definitions.meaning: in newspaper typesetting, to open up a page with more white space

explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street was the home of the London newspaper industry, so the first sense is a printing one.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter makes a page look less dense by opening it up, and unloading cargo makes something less heavy.

clue.text: Responsible person who stands for the good life?

definitions.text: Responsible person who stands for the good life?

parts.words: Responsible person who stands for the good life?
parts.note: a sponsor who stands up at a baptism and promises to guide the child in a godly life

explanation.walkthrough: 'stands for' suggests represents; at a christening the sponsor stands for the child.
explanation.definitionFit: A baptismal sponsor takes responsibility for a child's religious upbringing.

clue.text: Gibbon — talk about a master!

indicators.note: one word goes round the others, as if surrounding them

parts.note: to sing is slang for to talk to the police, to inform
MA is a Master of Arts

explanation.surface: An excited remark that a gibbon can chat to its master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and MA inside SING; to 'sing' is criminal slang for confessing or informing.
explanation.definitionFit: This large black ape of Sumatra and Malaysia is a species of gibbon.

clue.text: Tidy airport disrupted by the German intake

indicators.note: one word is broken open by the other piece, which sits in the middle of it

parts.note: Orly is one of the airports serving Paris
der is a German word for 'the'

explanation.surface: An airport thrown into chaos by an influx of Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'intake' reinforces the container: ORLY takes in DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something neat and well arranged is in good order.

clue.text: Measure of space and time

parts.note: a yard is an enclosed open space
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A gauge of space and time, as in physics.
explanation.definitionFit: A distance measured in yards, as in football gains, is a measurement.

clue.text: Brave young lad?

parts.note: not a courageous boy but the infant of a Native American warrior, known as a brave

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave' reads as an adjective; it is a noun for a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American Indian baby, the offspring of a brave, is known by this word.

clue.text: Expressions of contempt for Jack-of-all-trades

parts.note: pooh is a scornful exclamation
bah is a dismissive exclamation

explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, Pooh-Bah holds every office of state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mikado character holds many offices at once, so his name means someone with many jobs.

clue.text: Knocks return fight

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so the word for knocks is read backwards

parts.note: raps are sharp knocks

explanation.surface: A boxer takes blows and hits back in a rematch.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to box or fight in practice.

clue.text: Hence Queen -Bess taking leave

parts.note: Queen Elizabeth is ER, Elizabeth Regina
to go is to depart, take one's leave

explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is Latin for therefore, so it means consequently.

clue.text: Old county Scot

definitions.meaning: a former county of eastern Scotland, now a council area
a common Scottish man's name, standing for any Scotsman

explanation.walkthrough: Angus was a Scottish county before local government reorganisation.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Scottish shire shares its name with a typical Scottish forename.

clue.text: Commander of the Bounty?

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S ..., Union general in the American Civil War
a sum given freely, such as a subsidy

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Captain Bligh of HMS Bounty.
explanation.definitionFit: A Union general shares his name with a gift of money, a subsidy or award.

clue.text: Food left in a cooler

indicators.note: one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a fan cools the air

explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry case with a filling is a dish to eat.

clue.text: Perfect unit hand out

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one, a unit
to deal is to distribute, as cards

explanation.surface: A flawless unit hands out supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flawless is exactly as one would wish.

clue.text: Rebel on early plane going into hiding

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another comes after it

parts.note: AM means morning, early in the day
bus is old flying slang for an aeroplane
Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450

explanation.surface: An insurgent goes underground after catching a morning flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a 1450 English rebellion; 'bus' was RAF slang for an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a concealment of troops waiting to attack, a lying in hiding.

clue.text: Full of feeling for Red threatened with reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A communist under threat is offered reform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with reform' signals the anagram of RED and THREATENED.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind, compassionate person is easily moved and full of sympathy.
